what: Controlled vocabularies for ICMS v1. A spec, record or comparison may use only names defined here; adding a name is a change to this file, reviewed like code. Nothing here is a measurement.

phases.why: One exclusive phase list for every producer. The fourteen names of src/cryptanalysis/ic_measurement.rs plus isogeny, which cryptanalysis AGENTS.md T_cold charges and ic_measurement.rs lacks. Sum of the cold phases is T_cold; sum of the five online phases is T_online,1.

list.name: rho_solve
list.note: the reference arm's online interval, never part of an IC total

list.name: online_one_target
list.definition: AGENTS.md 'Primary comparison uses one target' and cryptanalysis AGENTS.md: start when target-dependent computation begins, after reusable target-independent setup is ready; stop after scalar recovery and independent verification. Exactly one target. Process launch, input loading and known-answer target construction are outside.

conformance.exact: the producer timed the five phases on exclusive clocks that sum to the online total (ic price --single-target, ic_measurement)
conformance.derived: the adapter assembled the interval from a producer's coarser phases; usable for operation counts, refused as a primary wall-clock speedup

list.name: cold_end_to_end
list.definition: AGENTS.md section 2: the whole method, cold, from setup to the recovered and verified logarithm, every phase charged. The unit S is defined over this window.

list.name: whole_process
list.definition: The measured child process from exec to exit, timed by the ICMS runner itself. Always available; includes start-up, input loading and report emission. A practicality figure, never a speedup.

list.name: stage_only
list.definition: One named phase or solver stage. A stage diagnostic (AGENTS.md section 2): never compared with a whole-pipeline window and never called a speedup.

units.why: AGENTS.md calls several different quantities 'S'. Each is a separate unit here, so a comparison across them is refused rather than silently made.

list.definition: ic bench / ic boundary: total group-addition equivalents / sqrt(r); native counters priced with docs/ic/calibration.json ratios.
list.deterministic: only when every native unit and every solver is priced by count (calibration_pins.measured empty and solver priced_by != measured)

list.definition: ic price: phase wall ns / ns of one batched add_many over 1,024 subgroup points, measured before and after each repetition; / sqrt(r).

list.deterministic: yes for a fixed binary, valgrind version and CPU feature dispatch

list.definition: experiments/ic-bench: exact counters weighted by frozen per-class batch-throughput weights (reference picoseconds). Runs under different calibration_id are never paired.
group additions and doublings, counted exactly; no conversion.
crypto-autoresearcher index_calculus: S3 root solves (one modular square root each).
CDCL conflicts. Comparable only for the same solver, version and search options (WDSat XG on/off changes conflicts by two orders of magnitude).
list.deterministic: yes for fixed solver, options and seed

list.definition: monotonic wall-clock nanoseconds of the declared window.
list.source: ICMS runner or the producer's exclusive clocks

list.definition: user+system CPU of the measured tree from wait4 rusage.

references.why: The rho reference moved three times between 2026-09-21 and 2026-10-01 (docs/ic/FRAMEWORK.md, BOUNDARY_TARGETS.md). A record names the reference it used; a comparison refuses two different names.

rho.status: before-mark only; never a reference since ledger section 18
reference for prime-field and random binary curves
Koblitz; the strong single-target walk is the admissibility minimum since 2026-10-01

rho.expected_ops: about sqrt(2*pi*r*k)/k per target for k targets
rho.status: historical diagnostic for k-target figures only; never the one-target reference
the producer's counted rho on the same subgroup and planted targets; the record carries its method string and automorphism count

factor_base_size_fields.why: The same names mean different things in different producers (docs/ic audit). ICMS records each separately and never lets one stand for another.

fields.usable_points: B in cryptanalysis AGENTS.md: distinct, nonidentity, subgroup-usable points before sign or Frobenius folding. This is the fb<B> of an IC1 candidate id.
fields.signed_points: points with P and -P both counted (ic bench signed_points).
fields.abscissae_with_points: distinct x carrying a point of the base (ic bench abscissae).
fields.abscissae_allowed: every x the construction admits, including those with no rational point (Koblitz pipeline abscissae).
fields.columns: unknowns in the relation matrix after folding (ic bench columns).
fields.nominal_dimension: the requested F_q-dimension of a subspace base; never a point count.

factor_base_families.why: Canonical family names, and how each producer spells them. An adapter refuses a family it has no spelling for.

list.means: points whose abscissa lies in an F_2-subspace V (Gaudry/Diem linear base)

param_notes.basis_law: which l-dimensional V, as cryptanalysis pdp-degree-heuristics/factor_base.py defines them; prefix is span{1, z, ..., z^(l-1)}, the literature's choice and crypto ic bench's only basis

optional_params.basis_seed: seed of the basis sampler for the randomised laws (cryptanalysis cell seed)

list.means: V a divisor submodule of T^n - 1 (KN-FIND-b9a41d); columns are signed Frobenius orbits
F_u = {P : 1/(x+1) in V}, T = (0,1) included, for the symmetrised oracle
union of Frobenius orbits of chosen seeds (not a subspace)
a parent base mapped into the prime-order subgroup by the cofactor
a parent base keeping only the listed abscissa orbits
a parent base closed under translation by rational 2-torsion
the legacy degree-ord_n(2) factor family, candidate by index
the smallest on-curve abscissae of a prime-field curve
abscissae x with x^d = g^d (multiplicative subgroup of F_p^*)
seed abscissae closed under the automorphism group of a CM curve
a frozen point list with its digest

pdp_metrics.why: The structural size of each point-decomposition system, so two solvers are compared on the same system. Unknown is null, never zero.

fields.n_vars: Boolean (or field) unknowns of the system as handed to the solver (SystemShape.n_vars)
fields.solving_degree: highest degree a Groebner/Macaulay engine reached
fields.anf_monomials: distinct monomials of the descended ANF
fields.cnf_clauses: clauses after encoding (ic corpus EncodingStats.clauses; ic_framework extra.original_clauses)

solver_options_that_change_search.why: Options that change a solver's counters by large factors. A spec must pin each one the solver has; a record that omits one is not comparable on that solver's counters.
